sources.entry: JSONExport - Desktop application for macOS which enables you to export JSON objects as model classes with their associated constructors, utility methods, setters and getters in your favorite language.

summary.one_liner: JSONExport is a Swift desktop app for macOS that converts JSON objects into model classes or structs for many languages and frameworks, with constructors, utility methods, and getters/setters.
summary.what_it_does: JSONExport takes a valid JSON object (or JSON array of objects) and generates model class files in one of 15 supported targets, including Java for Android, GSON, several Swift variants (classes, structures, CoreData, Realm, SwiftyJSON, Gloss, ObjectMapper, Unbox), and Objective-C variants for iOS, Mac, CoreData, and Realm. Users can set a root class name, a class name prefix, and a Java package name. Generated files can include a constructor that fills properties from a dictionary or JSON object, and a utility method that converts the object back to a dictionary; either, both, or neither can be chosen. The app offers a preview of generated content before saving. The README says the author is looking for new maintainers because they can no longer actively maintain the project.
use_cases: generate Swift model structs from an API response
create Java or GSON classes for an Android app from JSON
convert JSON to Realm or CoreData models
scaffold Objective-C model classes for iOS
preview generated model code before saving
bootstrap typed models from sample JSON
how_to_run: Build it using Xcode 8 or later.
notable: Supports 15 output targets across Java, Swift, and Objective-C
Can generate constructors and utility methods (to dictionary) separately or together
Can open .json files and handle JSON arrays of objects
Root class name, class prefix, and Java package name are configurable
caveats: The author is seeking new maintainers and says they cannot actively maintain the project or respond to all issues
Runs only on macOS; built with Xcode
Known limitations: CoreData cannot represent arrays of strings, Realm primitives need manual defaults, empty JSON values cannot be typed, and deeply nested arrays/objects are not exported correctly
